summary: In this story, fishermen and a group of schoolchildren on a research trip help marine biologists calmly guide a confused young whale back to the open sea.
introduce: Show the title “The Whale Who Lost Its Way” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: a steady flow of water moving in one direction
unable to think clearly or know what to do
careful study done to learn new facts about something

challengeTerms.def: a scientist who studies living things
relating to sound or the sense of hearing
to find and follow a path or direction, especially when traveling

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that helping a lost wild animal is always worth the time and effort? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how teamwork and patience helped guide the lost whale back to the open sea.
struggling: Pre-teach current, confused, and research with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses biologist, acoustic, and navigate to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
